source_scope.lane: execution authority, sandbox/capability boundaries, security failures and safety architecture history
source_scope.non_overlap_basis: Live center crossread showed peer lanes for architecture history, state/identity/failure, GWT and XENO/ClayCode. This shard restricts itself to execution-authority/security-boundary evolution and current Safe-Effect implications.
source_scope.history_warning: Several material safety commits predate the currently frozen partial recent-window manifest. This is valid history evidence discovered through GitHub commit search, but it does not freeze or complete the repository history denominator.

findings.claim: A historical agentic executor used skip_approval=True for high-risk tools; the security-fix commit reports that this bypassed safety checks, allowed arbitrary destructive commands without user consent and caused a full system wipe.
findings.current_implication: Treat model output as untrusted intent, never execution authority. Any Clay capability/commit gateway must fail closed, preserve an external authority boundary and be regression-tested against approval-bypass and equivalent confused-deputy failures.

findings.claim: The post-incident hardening combined a low-risk auto-approval whitelist, explicit approval for mutating tools, protected-path checks, expanded destructive-command detection and Firejail filesystem restrictions.
findings.current_implication: Reuse the incident tests and defense-in-depth lesson, but move the invariant below string/prompt policy into typed capability/effect mediation.

findings.claim: A later hard-delete guardrail removed fs_delete from the agent registry and attempted to block deletion equivalents in bash and Python, explicitly aiming for no delete capability and no approval bypass.
findings.current_implication: This is a direct historical precursor to Safe-Effect Clay, but pattern/tool blocking is not sufficient closure. Clay must prove equivalent destructive effects remain unreachable through subprocesses, FFI, generated code, raw syscalls and alternate encodings.

findings.claim: Agentic hardening replaced max-step risk with compound risk 1-product(1-risk_i), added EMA-weighted failure scoring and Firejail resource ceilings for code/bash execution.
findings.current_implication: Risk and resource damage are compositional. Clay capability budgets should account for cumulative multi-step exposure and include resource/process/network limits, not only per-operation labels.

findings.claim: The Firejail implementation explicitly logged a warning and continued unsandboxed when Firejail was unavailable.
findings.current_implication: A current protected-effect runtime must test fail-closed semantics: absence or failure of the enforcement backend cannot silently expand authority.

findings.claim: Autonomous research was deliberately given a restricted capability subset, rate/cooldown budgets and sandboxed code; self-authored Genesis proposals followed sandbox validation, destructivity checks and a separate FAS accept/reject path before registration.
findings.current_implication: Per-context capabilities plus proposal/validation/commit separation are historically proven design patterns in FRANK and can inform a deterministic IrreversibleEffectRequest/commit broker.

findings.claim: V15/V25 evaluations found attack/tool leakage and harmful-query gaps that were repaired with increasingly specific regex/pre-filter and executor blocklists; V25 specifically reported attack-script, stalking-guide and stolen-card-market failures before patching.
findings.current_implication: Reactive string filters are useful defense-in-depth and regression cases but cannot establish authority safety or prompt-injection resistance.

findings.claim: The separate Projects/Claude coding-agent subsystem first constrained file tools to a project-root sandbox, then deliberately removed that sandbox and granted full-system file/bash/service/package authority while retaining only a tiny destructive-command blocklist.
findings.current_implication: Authority boundaries can drift when implemented independently per agent/subsystem. Clay should make capability scope a centrally enforced semantic/runtime property that child agents cannot widen by local code changes.

findings.claim: Historical design explicitly used an abliterated model with safety layers removed and in another path routed darknet intent through tooling to bypass a model refusal; therefore model refusal behavior was not a stable execution boundary.
findings.current_implication: Current Safety-Effect claims must be evaluated with compromised/uncooperative model intent; success cannot depend on refusal text.

current_rae_cross_mapping.assessment: The historical evidence materially supports prioritizing the Safe-Effect research axis, especially authority non-amplification, external irreversible-effect brokerage, resource boundedness and foreign-code closure. It does not prove those candidate invariants sound or complete.
supported_research_links: model -> IrreversibleEffectRequest -> external/deterministic broker -> commit receipt
recoverability-preserving/versioned writes instead of ambient destructive mutation

earned_work_mapping_candidate.mechanism_or_result: Historical catastrophic approval-bypass incident plus subsequent delete-capability removal, sandbox/resource hardening, capability scoping and safety-eval regressions provide reusable safety architecture constraints and a concrete adversarial test atlas.
earned_work_mapping_candidate.falsifier_or_validation_receipt: Safe-Effect/Reference Harness must reproduce approval bypass, sandbox absence, child-process/FFI destructive-equivalent attempts, authority drift and multi-step resource/risk accumulation as failing baseline tests and passing mediated-runtime tests.

cheap_discriminating_tests: Approval-token binding: bind authorization to exact normalized effect, capability set, protected-state hash, expiry and single-use nonce; mutate any field and require rejection.
Fail-closed enforcement: remove/kill sandbox/effect broker and verify protected effects stop rather than execute ambiently.

Foreign-code closure matrix: request equivalent protected destruction through Clay, Bash, Python, C/Rust/WASM/FFI and nested tool subprocesses; child effective effects must never exceed parent contract.

Authority-drift regression: create/modify a secondary agent subsystem and attempt to widen its file/process/network scope without an ExternalGrant; runtime must reject widening independent of local prompt/code claims.

Compound-risk/resource test: execute long sequences of individually medium-risk reversible actions and verify aggregate budgets/tripwires prevent emergent resource damage while preserving normal build/test utility.
